# Services and capabilities

> Caligrafy Quill 2.25.0. Generated from the source by `php qa/build-api-reference.php`; the guides explain how to use these classes, this reference says exactly what each public method takes and returns. Back to the [API reference](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Reference).

Build once: services, the capability registry, errors, the container, personal access tokens and the audit log.

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`Caligrafy\Service`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#service) | Extend it in application/services/, declare the inputs and implement handle() |
| [`Caligrafy\Capability`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capability) | #[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book to the catalog', scope: 'books:write')] on a class that extends Caligrafy\Service. |
| [`Caligrafy\Capabilities`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#capabilities) | A capability is a class of application/services/ that extends Service and carries #[Capability(...)]. |
| [`Caligrafy\ServiceError`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#serviceerror) | A service throws it to refuse a call. |
| [`Caligrafy\Container`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#container) | Capabilities are made by the container, so a service asks for what it uses in its constructor |
| [`Caligrafy\Tokens`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#tokens) | A token is `cq_<id>_<secret>`: shown once when it is created, stored only as a SHA-256 hash in caligrafy_tokens with a name, an optional owner (users.id), its scopes, an optional expiry, the last use and a revocation ... |
| [`Caligrafy\Audit`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Capabilities#audit) | One row per capability call that changes data, and per refused call: when, who (a user, a token, the CLI), through which channel, which capability and the outcome. |

<a name="service"></a>
## abstract class Caligrafy\Service

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

abstract class Service
```

Source: [framework/core/Service.php:34](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Service.php#L34)

Class Service
Extend it in application/services/, declare the inputs and implement handle():

```
#[Capability(name: 'create_book', description: 'Adds a book', scope: 'books:write')]
class CreateBook extends Service {
    public $rules = ['title' => 'required|max_len,255', 'author_id' => 'required|integer'];
    public $filters = ['title' => 'trim|sanitize_string'];
    public $descriptions = ['title' => 'The title of the book'];
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        return (new Book('books'))->create($input);
    }
}
```

- $rules: GUMP validation rules per input. Only the inputs listed here reach handle(); use '' for an input without a rule. They also give the JSON Schema that agents and clients see (Capabilities::schema()). A file input takes the rule 'file' (2.19.0): 'cover' =&gt; 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'. Web pages and REST save the uploaded file and give handle() its public URL; MCP and the command line send a URL or a path (Caligrafy\Uploads).
- $filters: GUMP filters applied before validation.
- handle() returns data (an array, a model, a list of models, a scalar) and throws ServiceError to refuse. It never renders a view, redirects, prints or reads the request or the session: the context says who calls.

### Public properties

+ `public $rules = array()`: array input =&gt; GUMP rules
+ `public $filters = array()`: array input =&gt; GUMP filters
+ `public $descriptions = array()`: array input =&gt; description, for the schema

Attribute Capability

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#capability-construct)

<a name="capability-construct"></a>
#### `->__construct()`

```php
public function __construct(
    public string $name,
    public string $description = '',
    public string $scope = '',
    public int $level = 0,
    public bool $readOnly = false,
    public bool $destructive = false,
    public bool $public = false,
    public bool $mcp = true,
    public bool $webOnly = false,
    public bool $async = false
)
```

**Parameters**

+ `$name` `string`: snake_case, unique in the application (create_book)
+ `$description` `string`, default `''`: one or two sentences: what it does and returns (shown to agents as the tool description)
+ `$scope` `string`, default `''`: the token scope it needs (books:write); '' = any token
+ `$level` `int`, default `0`: the minimum value of the users permission column (0 = any signed-in user)
+ `$readOnly` `bool`, default `false`: true when it changes nothing (not audited when it succeeds; agents may call it freely)
+ `$destructive` `bool`, default `false`: true when it deletes or overwrites data (agents ask before calling it)
+ `$public` `bool`, default `false`: true when anyone may call it without signing in or a token
+ `$mcp` `bool`, default `true`: false keeps it out of the MCP tools (one only a browser can use, such as a push subscription)
+ `$webOnly` `bool`, default `false`: true (2.21.0): only Route::action() reaches it: it may read the session and sign people in
+ `$async` `bool`, default `false`

Source: [framework/core/Capability.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Capability.php#L30)

<a name="capabilities"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Capabilities

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Capabilities
```

Source: [framework/core/Capabilities.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Capabilities.php#L22)

Class Capabilities
A capability is a class of application/services/ that extends Service and carries #[Capability(...)].
Every channel calls it through call(), which always does the same, in order:
1. finds it (not_found)
2. checks the context: public, or signed in / a token (unauthenticated), with the scope and level (forbidden)
3. keeps, filters and validates the declared inputs (invalid)
4. runs handle()
5. writes the audit log: every refusal, and every success of a capability that is not read-only
and returns plain data (models become arrays of their columns).

<a name="container"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Container

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Container
```

Source: [framework/core/Container.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Container.php#L25)

Class Container (2.18.0)
Capabilities are made by the container, so a service asks for what it uses in its constructor:

```
public function __construct(private Mailer $mailer) {}
```

A class the container has no binding for is built with its constructor's parameters resolved the same way (a class
or interface type -&gt; Container::get, else the parameter's default). Bindings go in application/config/container.php:

```
Container::singleton(PaymentGateway::class, fn () => new StripeGateway(getenv('STRIPE_SECRET')));
Container::bind(Clock::class, SystemClock::class);
```

A test swaps one with Container::instance(Mailer::class, $fake), then Container::reset() forgets it.

### Constants

+ `FILE = 'config/container.php'`

+ [`Container::has()`](#container-has)

+ [`Container::make()`](#container-make)
+ [`Container::boot()`](#container-boot)
+ [`Container::reset()`](#container-reset)

<a name="tokens"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Tokens

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Tokens
```

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:19](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L19)

Class Tokens
A token is `cq_<id>_<secret>`: shown once when it is created, stored only as a SHA-256 hash in caligrafy_tokens
with a name, an optional owner (users.id), its scopes, an optional expiry, the last use and a revocation date.

Scopes are `<resource>:<action>` strings (books:read, books:write). A token scope `*` grants everything and
`books:*` grants every action on books. Tables: framework/settings/platform.sql (php caligrafer.php platform install).

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_tokens'`
+ `PREFIX = 'cq_'`

### Methods

+ [`Tokens::create()`](#tokens-create)
+ [`Tokens::verify()`](#tokens-verify)
+ [`Tokens::expired()`](#tokens-expired)
+ [`Tokens::expiresAt()`](#tokens-expiresat)
+ [`Tokens::revoke()`](#tokens-revoke)
+ [`Tokens::all()`](#tokens-all)
+ [`Tokens::installed()`](#tokens-installed)
+ [`Tokens::looksLikeToken()`](#tokens-looksliketoken)
+ [`Tokens::parse()`](#tokens-parse)
+ [`Tokens::allows()`](#tokens-allows)
+ [`Tokens::normalizeScopes()`](#tokens-normalizescopes)

<a name="tokens-create"></a>
#### `Tokens::create()`

```php
public static function create($name, $scopes = array(), $userId = null, $expiresAt = null)
```

Creates a token

**Parameters**

+ `$name` `string`: what the token is for ("Claude Code on my laptop")
+ `$scopes` `array`, default `array()`: the scopes it grants
+ `$userId` `int|null`, default `null`: the user it acts for (null: the application itself)
+ `$expiresAt` `int|string|null`, default `null`: a Unix time (time() + 86400 * 90), or a local 'Y-m-d H:i:s' (null: never expires)

**Returns** `array`: ['id' =&gt; ..., 'token' =&gt; 'cq_...']: the token is never shown again

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:32](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L32)

+ `$now` `int|null`, default `null`: a Unix time (null: now)

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:78](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L78)

<a name="tokens-expiresat"></a>
#### `Tokens::expiresAt()`

```php
public static function expiresAt($expiresAt)
```

The expires_at value of an expiry given as a Unix time. Dates are stored in local time (SERVER_TIMEZONE), and when
the clocks fall back the repeated hour names two instants: strtotime() reads its first one. A token created at
01:21 EDT to expire an hour later (01:21 EST) would be refused at once, so an instant of the second occurrence
is stored as the first local time after the repeated hour (02:00): it never stops early, at worst an hour late.

**Parameters**

+ `$expiresAt` `int|string|null`: a Unix time, a local 'Y-m-d H:i:s' (kept as given) or null (never expires)

**Returns** `string|null`

Source: [framework/core/Tokens.php:95](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Tokens.php#L95)

<a name="audit"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Audit

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Audit
```

Source: [framework/core/Audit.php:17](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Audit.php#L17)

Class Audit
One row per capability call that changes data, and per refused call: when, who (a user, a token, the CLI),
through which channel, which capability and the outcome. Inputs are never stored.
Without the table (php caligrafer.php platform install) nothing is written and nothing fails.

### Constants

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_audit'`

### Methods

+ [`Audit::record()`](#audit-record)
+ [`Audit::latest()`](#audit-latest)


Records one call

**Parameters**

+ `$context` `Context`: who called and through which channel
+ `$capability` `string`: the capability name
+ `$outcome` `string`: ok, invalid, unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict, error
+ `$detail` `string|null`, default `null`: a short note (an error message), at most 500 characters

**Returns** `bool`: whether the row was written
